title: Dependency Injection: Separating Responsibilities
content:
Dependency Injection separates a class from the responsibility of creating its dependencies. Instead of a class knowing how to handle CSV, JSON, and XML directly, those implementations can be provided at runtime.

Without DI, centralized logic can be perfectly reasonable when the functionality is small, stable, and naturally belongs together. The problem appears when a class accumulates too many responsibilities, especially format-specific logic and growing if/else branches.

DI becomes useful when responsibilities need to change independently, when implementations may be substituted, or when a component needs to be tested in isolation.

DI is not a rule to avoid every new statement or create an interface for every class. If centralized logic is simpler, keep it centralized. Use DI when it provides a real separation or testing benefit.
